title: SIU probing fatal shooting by police
article: About 50 witnesses have been interviewed by the Special Investigations Unit as the civilian unit continues its probe into a fatal police shooting Sunday.

Police shot Mark Norman Graham, 38, to death in front of a crowded doughnut shop. An autopsy is expected to be performed today. Graham had been wanted in connection with an earlier shooting of Raymond (Frenchy) Taillefer, 39, who was shot at close range outside a local bar.
It's a hard time for us and not knowing the police side of it it's even harder," said Mark's father Doug Graham.

Police repeatedly asked Graham to lay down his bags Sunday at about 2:15 p.m. He refused as he walked away from police toward Tim Hortons. Witnesses said he reached for his bag and started to turn around when three shots were fired by police.
A mob of people appeared just moments before the shooting, alternately heckling Graham and encouraging him to defy police.
A lot of people were calling him names - foul names," said Lance Hemelaar, 31.
Some teenagers goaded him to ignore the police.
At the Tim Hortons where the shooting occurred, conversation yesterday continued to revolve around the shooting.
It's still fresh," said customer Millie Barrett, who drops by the coffee shop daily. It's frightening in a small town."
You think when you come to a small town, you are safer than when you're in a big city," added Cindy Pereira. But when something like this happens you don't know where to go anymore."
